title: PEO for Small Business: Benefits, Costs, and How to Choose One
summary: A PEO gives a small business access to big-company benefits, HR expertise, and compliance support through a co-employment model. This guide explains how a PEO works, what it costs, what it does and doesn't support, and how to choose one. You'll leave able to judge whether a PEO fits your business.
body_markdown:
You're doing everything right. Your team is growing, revenue is climbing, and you're finally seeing the business you built start to take off.


Then the HR reality hits.


Benefits renewals with confusing insurance jargon. Payroll tax filings for a new hire in a new state you're not sure you're handling correctly. An employee asking how to file for FMLA, and you're Googling it in real time. Another one wondering why your health plan costs so much more than their friends at a bigger company.


When you started your business, you didn’t expect to also have to become an HR expert. But somewhere along the way, that became part of the job, and it's eating up time you don't have.


A Professional Employer Organization (PEO) is designed to help alleviate some of the administrative burden that may be on your shoulders. It gives small businesses access to the benefits, HR expertise, payroll administration, and compliance support that larger companies have in-house without having to build all of it yourself.


This article walks you through how a PEO works, what it costs, what it does and doesn't support, and how to choose one that fits your business. Read on to get a clearer picture of whether a PEO is the right move, or if another option makes more sense for where you are today.


## What is a PEO and how does it work?


A PEO is an HR provider that works with your small business through a co-employment arrangement. They help handle HR administration, payroll, benefits access, and compliance support while you continue to run your business and manage your team.


**Here's how co-employment works in practice:**


**You retain control over:**


- Hiring and firing and workforce decisions
- Employee pay rates and job roles
- Day-to-day management and culture
- Business operations and strategy


**The PEO helps handle:**


- Payroll processing and tax administration
- Access and administration of employee benefits (health, dental, vision, retirement)
- HR compliance support (employment-related rules and requirements, filings, best practices)
- Workers' compensation insurance and claims
- Risk mitigation support and employment practices liability insurance ([EPLI](https://www.investopedia.com/what-is-employment-practices-liability-coverage-8348723) )


Within a co-employment model, a PEO may serve as the employer of record for certain payroll tax purposes.


The PEO offers access to PEO-sponsored plans. This allows your employees access to large-group benefit plans typically reserved for much bigger companies. But you're still the boss. You're still running the show. The PEO just supports the administrative backend that would otherwise generally be supported by a full HR department.


**For a deeper look at the mechanics, see**[what a PEO is](https://www.trinet.com/insights/what-is-a-peo) **and**[how co-employment works](https://www.trinet.com/insights/how-co-employment-works-setting-expectations) **.**


## Why use a PEO for your small business?


A PEO can help a growing small business compete for talent, reduce administrative burden, and mitigate risk, without the cost and complexity of building an internal HR function.


According to the National Association of Professional Employer Organizations ([NAPEO](https://napeo.org/intro-to-peos/industry-research-data/#:~:text=Businesses%20hiring%20a%20PEO%20grow%20twice%20as%20fast%2C,a%20PEO%2C%20in%20cost%20savings%20alone%2C%20is%2027%25.) ), businesses that work with PEOs grow 7-9% faster, have 10-14% lower employee turnover, and are 50% less likely to go out of business compared to similar-sized businesses that don't use a PEO.

## Here's what a PEO typically provides.


### Cost-effective access to benefits


One of the biggest advantages of working with a PEO is access to large-group health, dental, and vision plans that small businesses may not be able to sponsor on their own.


That means your team gets access to benefits similar to those that may be offered by big companies, without the added cost of building a dedicated HR team or investing in specialized software to manage it all yourself.


### Employee benefits administration


[Open enrollment](https://www.trinet.com/hr-glossary/open-enrollment) ,[COBRA](https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/health-plans/cobra) notices, life event change events,[FSA](https://www.fsafeds.gov/) reconciliation—benefits administration is time-consuming and detail-heavy. A PEO administers the process, so you're not chasing down paperwork or troubleshooting benefits-related issues.


Employees get access to self-service tools where they can review plan options, make elections, and update information, reducing the load on you and your team.


### Access to HR expertise


Most small businesses don't have a dedicated HR team. A PEO gives you access to HR professionals who can help with employee relations, compliance questions, policy development, performance management, and separation best practices.


Instead of Googling "how to handle a harassment complaint" at 9 p.m., you can call someone whose expertise is HR for information and best practices. This expertise helps companies stay up to date of ever-changing local, state, and federal employment-related rules and requirements and can help you navigate compliance challenges before they become potential costly problems.


For more on how HR outsourcing can support your business, see[advantages of HR outsourcing](https://www.trinet.com/insights/8-advantages-of-human-resources-outsourcing) .


### Risk management and EPLI


Employment-related claims (wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, etc.) can be overwhelming and financially devastating for a small business. Many PEOs, including[TriNet PEO](https://www.trinet.com/peo) , include employment practices liability insurance (EPLI) as part of their service. TriNet provides a $1 million EPLI policy to help protect your business from costly claims and lawsuits. Beyond the insurance, leading PEOs like TriNet guide you through the process of handling an employment claim and provide best practices and resources to help mitigate employment-related risks.


A PEO can also help you stay up to date of[HR compliance](https://www.trinet.com/peo/capabilities) by tracking federal, state, and local employment-related rules and requirements changes and helping you with your policies accordingly. They also typically offer workers' compensation programs and help facilitate claims management, along with training and workplace safety assessments.


### Payroll and tax administration


A[PEO helps you process payroll](https://www.trinet.com/peo/capabilities) , withholds and remits payroll taxes, files reports, administers year-end[W-2s](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-2) , and supports multi-state payroll complexities. If you're growing into new states or dealing with local tax jurisdictions, a PEO can help you navigate compliance without hiring specialists.


Beyond just processing support, PEOs provide compliance support with ever-changing payroll tax laws and employment-related requirements. This can be especially helpful for businesses dealing with multi-state payroll or payroll challenges that come with their own payroll tax complications.


### Self-service technology


Most[PEOs offer cloud-based platforms](https://www.trinet.com/peo/technology) where employees can access pay stubs, request time off, update personal information, view benefits information, and complete onboarding tasks. These self-service portals empower employees to independently manage their data, leading to fewer HR inquiries and minimized manual data entry tasks.


Managers get tools for approvals, reporting, and performance tracking all in one system. With 24/7 accessibility, these online platforms cater to the dynamic schedules of modern workforces and help streamline HR functions while enhancing employee autonomy.


### Training and development


Many PEOs provide access to[employee training programs](https://www.trinet.com/hr-services/technology-platform/training-and-learning-management) , compliance courses (harassment prevention, workplace safety), leadership development workshops, and professional skills courses. Depending on the contract, PEOs might offer a vast array of training materials, online courses, and professional development resources tailored to various industries and roles.


This helps ensure employees remain skilled, aids in career advancement, and boosts morale and retention, all making it easier for SMBs to offer robust training opportunities without managing the full program on their own.


How much does a PEO cost?


Pricing Model How It Works


Percentage of payroll


The PEO charges a percentage of your gross payroll each pay period. The percentage can vary significantly depending on the scope of services and your business profile.


Per-employee-per-month (PEPM)


A flat monthly fee for each employee, regardless of pay. This model can offer more predictable budgeting since the cost doesn't fluctuate with pay changes.


TriNet uses transparent per-employee-per-month admin pricing, which makes budgeting more predictable and can help eliminate surprises when payroll fluctuates due to bonuses, commissions, or seasonal pay changes. You can explore how TriNet pricing works at[TriNet PEO pricing](https://www.trinet.com/peo/pricing) **.**


**Examples of what may be included and what may cost extra**


**Most PEO fees cover:**


- Payroll processing and tax administration
- Access to health, dental, and vision plans (though you and employees still pay premiums)
- HR support and compliance guidance
- Workers' compensation insurance
- EPLI coverage (varies by provider)


**You’ll likely still pay for:**


- Employee wages and salaries and hourly rates (the PEO doesn't reduce payroll costs)
- Health insurance costs (can be shared between you and employees)
- Retirement plan contributions (if you offer a 401(k))
- Taxes themselves (the PEO administers them, but the payroll tax liability is still yours)


**Fees to watch for**


**Some PEOs charge additional fees for:**


- Implementation and onboarding
- Per-transaction fees (adding/removing employees, running off-cycle payrolls)
- State registration fees for workers' comp or unemployment insurance
- Premium add-ons (expanded EPLI limits, additional training, custom reporting)


Ask up front what's included in the base price and what's billed separately **.**


## What a PEO does not do


A PEO is a provider, not a replacement for leadership. Here's what stays with you:


**You retain full control over:**


- Hiring and firing and workforce decisions
- Setting employee pay rates and job roles
- Day-to-day supervision and performance management
- Company culture, values, and strategy
- Business operations and client relationships


**A PEO is not:**


- A staffing agency (it doesn't find or place employees for you)
- A business manager (it doesn't run your operations)
- A cost eliminator for wages or taxes (you still pay employees and cover tax liabilities the PEO just administers them)


Understanding this up front helps set realistic expectations. A PEO supports the administrative and compliance backend so you can focus on running and growing your business, but the people decisions and business direction remain yours.


## How to choose a PEO for your small business


**Not all PEOs are created equal. Here's what to look for when evaluating providers:**


### ESAC Accreditation


TriNet complies with all ESAC standards and maintain ESAC accreditation since 1995.


[View accreditation](https://www.peoreliability.org/TriNetGroup)


The Employer Services Assurance Corporation (ESAC) independently audits PEOs for financial stability, regulatory compliance, and ethical business practices. ESAC accreditation is a signal that the PEO meets rigorous industry standards.


**TriNet has maintained ESAC accreditation since 1995.**


### Benefit plan quality and carrier network


Ask which health insurance carriers the PEO works with, what plan types are available (HMO, PPO, HDHP), and whether the plans include access to robust networks in your area. A PEO's value often hinges on the robustness of the benefit plans it can offer.


### Service model and support


Some PEOs assign you a dedicated HR consultant. Others use a call center or ticketing system. Understand how you'll get support when you need it, and whether the service model matches your expectations.


### Pricing transparency


Ask for a clear breakdown of what's included in the base fee and what costs extra. If a PEO can't or won't give you a straight answer on pricing, that's a red flag.


### Industry experience


Some PEOs specialize in specific industries (tech, healthcare, nonprofits, manufacturing). If your business has unique compliance needs or workforce dynamics, it's worth working with a PEO that understands your space.


For a detailed evaluation checklist, see[11 questions to ask before choosing a PEO](https://www.trinet.com/insights/11-questions-to-ask-before-choosing-a-peo) .


## Is a PEO right for your business?


### A PEO tends to be a strong fit if:


✔ You have 5-100+ employees and growing
✔ You want to offer compressive premium benefits than you can access on your own
✔ You don't have a dedicated HR team (or person)
✔ You're expanding into new states and need multi-state payroll and compliance support
✔ You want to reduce administrative burden so you can focus on running the business
✔ You're in an industry with unique workers' comp or employment-related considerations


### A PEO may not be the best fit if:


✘ You have fewer than 5 employees (the cost-to-value ratio may not justify it yet)
✘ You prefer to keep all HR functions in-house, do not want to use technology, and have your staff to administer it
✘ You're in a very high-risk industry where PEOs may not accept you or charge prohibitively high workers' comp rates


If you're not quite ready for a PEO, an alternative like[TriNet HR Plus](https://www.trinet.com/hr-plus) may be a better fit. HR Plus is an Administrative Services Organization (ASO) model that gives you access to HR support, payroll, benefits administration, and compliance tools without the co-employment structure.


Not sure which model fits? Use the[HR solution assessment tool](https://www.trinet.com/resources/tools/hr-solution-assessment) to see which path makes sense for your business stage and needs.


## PEO vs other options


Here's how a PEO stacks up against other HR solutions small businesses commonly consider:


Solution What It Supports Best For


PEO


Payroll, benefits access, HR, compliance, workers' comp, EPLI


Growing businesses (5-500 employees) wanting big-company benefits and full HR support


Payroll company


Payroll processing, tax filing


Businesses that just need payroll services and can manage HR and benefits separately


HR software


Tools for payroll, time tracking, onboarding, document storage


Businesses with internal HR staff who need technology to manage processes


ASO (like TriNet HR Plus)


Payroll, benefits administration, HR tools, and support without co-employment


Businesses that want flexibility and support but prefer to retain full employer-of-record status and sponsor their own benefits


Each model has trade-offs. A PEO offers the most comprehensive support but requires a co-employment relationship. An ASO offers flexibility without co-employment. Payroll companies and HR software are lighter-touch tools that assume you have more internal HR capacity.


## Frequently Asked Questions


What does PEO stand for?


PEO stands for Professional Employer Organization. A PEO works with your business through a co-employment relationship, becoming the employer of record for payroll tax purposes and you retain control over workforce and business decisions, hiring, separations, pay, and day-to-day management.


How much does a PEO cost?


A good example of what most PEOs cost is 2-12% of your total payroll or a flat per-employee-per-month fee ranging from $60 to $250+ per employee, depending on services, employee count, and business complexity. TriNet uses transparent per-employee-per-month admin pricing for more predictable budgeting. See the How much does a PEO cost? section above for details.


Is a PEO worth it for a small business?


For many small businesses, a PEO can be worth the investment, especially if you want to offer competitive benefits, reduce HR administrative burden, and mitigate HR risk without adding an internal HR team. According to NAPEO, businesses that use PEOs tend to grow 7-9% faster, retain employees 10-14% longer, and are 50% less likely to go out of business. Whether it's worth it depends on your employee count, growth stage, and how much time you're currently spending on HR tasks.


What is the difference between a PEO and a payroll company?


A payroll company processes payroll and files payroll taxes, but that's typically where the service ends. A PEO supports payroll and gives you access to employee benefits, HR expertise, compliance support, workers' comp insurance, and EPLI coverage. If you just need payroll services, a payroll company may be enough. If you need comprehensive HR support, a PEO is the more complete solution.


## A PEO can help you compete and grow without building out an HR department


As your business and your team grow, the HR administrative load grows with it and it can quickly overwhelm you if you're trying to handle it all yourself.


A PEO gives small businesses access to benefits, expertise, and compliance support that help them compete for talent, mitigate against risk, and stay focused on growth. It's not the right fit for every business, but for companies in that 5-100+ employee range looking to scale without adding internal HR headcount, a PEO can offer meaningful advantages.
